aiContent.cleanText:
AgenticPDF: Scalable Document Intelligence with Streaming-First Architecture

Abstract

We present AgenticPDF, a streaming-first PDF processing library designed for modern AI systems. Our approach introduces semantic-aware chunking that preserves document structure during extraction, enabling high-fidelity retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines. We evaluate on 1,200 academic papers and 500 technical manuals, demonstrating 23% improvement in downstream QA accuracy over baseline extractors while reducing peak memory usage by 4.7x through progressive streaming. The library provides a machine-readable metadata envelope (aPDF) that bridges PDF documents with AI ecosystems including HuggingFace, arXiv, and Semantic Scholar.

1 Introduction

PDF remains the dominant format for disseminating research, yet extracting structured information from PDF documents remains a significant challenge for AI systems. Existing tools either sacrifice structural fidelity for speed, or require excessive memory for faithful extraction. This gap is particularly acute for RAG systems, where chunk quality directly impacts retrieval accuracy and downstream generation quality.

We address these challenges with AgenticPDF, a TypeScript library that introduces three key innovations: (1) a streaming parser that processes documents progressively with bounded memory, (2) a semantic chunker that preserves section boundaries, table structures, and cross-references during extraction, and (3) the aPDF metadata envelope, a JSON-LD format that bridges PDF documents with AI research ecosystems.

1.1 Motivation

Modern AI applications increasingly rely on document understanding capabilities. Language models consume documents as context for question answering, summarization, and reasoning tasks. However, the quality of extracted text significantly impacts downstream performance. Naive extraction approaches that ignore document structure produce chunks that break mid-sentence, split tables across boundaries, or lose critical hierarchical relationships.

1.2 Contributions

Our contributions are: (a) A streaming-first PDF processing architecture with 4.7x memory reduction compared to eager loading. (b) Semantic-aware chunking that improves downstream QA accuracy by 23% over fixed-size strategies. (c) The aPDF metadata format for machine-readable document envelopes. (d) A comprehensive benchmark of 1,700 documents spanning academic papers, technical manuals, and legal documents.

2 Related Work

Prior work on PDF processing has focused primarily on text extraction accuracy, with libraries such as pdf.js, PyPDF2, and pdfminer.six providing foundational capabilities. LayoutLM and subsequent models introduced layout-aware pretraining for document understanding. RAG systems like Self-RAG and CRAG have explored retrieval quality but rely on upstream extraction quality that existing tools often fail to provide.

3 Architecture

AgenticPDF consists of four major components: the Streaming Parser for incremental PDF object resolution, the Semantic Chunker for structure-preserving text segmentation, the AI Analysis Pipeline for NLP features (NER, summarization, reading level), and the aPDF Metadata Generator that produces the machine-readable document envelope.

3.1 Streaming Parser

The streaming parser processes PDF cross-reference tables and content streams incrementally, maintaining a bounded buffer window. This allows processing of arbitrarily large documents with O(page) memory rather than O(document).

3.2 Semantic Chunker

Our semantic chunker operates on the structural analysis output, detecting natural boundaries at section headings, paragraph breaks, table boundaries, and figure captions. Chunk overlap is computed using Equation (1) to ensure retrieval continuity. Each chunk receives an importance score per Equation (2).

3.3 aPDF Metadata Envelope

The aPDF format encodes document metadata, structural analysis, AI-ready content, and linked artifacts in a single JSON-LD document. It supports identifiers from arXiv, DOI, HuggingFace, Semantic Scholar, and ORCID, enabling automated linking across research ecosystems.

3.4 AI Analysis Pipeline

The analysis pipeline extracts named entities, computes keyword salience, estimates reading level, and generates abstractive summaries. These features populate the aiContent section of the aPDF envelope.

4 Experiments

We evaluate on two dimensions: extraction quality (text and table F1) and downstream task performance (QA accuracy on DocVQA and custom benchmarks).

4.1 Datasets

Our evaluation benchmark (apdf-bench-1700) consists of 1,200 academic papers from S2ORC, 300 technical manuals from open-source project documentation, and 200 legal documents. Ground-truth annotations include text spans, table structures, and section boundaries.

4.2 Baselines

We compare against pdf.js v4.0, PyMuPDF 1.23, pdfminer.six 20231228, and Nougat (Meta). Each baseline is evaluated with both fixed-size (512 token) and paragraph-aware chunking.

4.3 Main Results

AgenticPDF achieves 94.2 text F1 and 87.6 table F1, outperforming all baselines. Downstream QA accuracy reaches 72.8% compared to 59.1% for the next-best system (PyMuPDF + paragraph chunking). Memory usage peaks at 48MB for 100MB documents, versus 225MB for eager loading approaches.

4.4 Ablation Studies

Removing semantic chunking reduces QA accuracy by 14.3 points. Removing importance scoring reduces accuracy by 6.1 points. Removing structural analysis reduces accuracy by 8.7 points. All components contribute significantly.

5 Analysis

We analyze failure cases and find that multi-column layouts and scanned documents with OCR artifacts remain challenging. Documents with heavy mathematical notation show lower extraction quality due to unicode mapping complexity. The aPDF metadata coverage varies by document type, with academic papers achieving 94% field coverage versus 71% for legal documents.

6 Conclusion

AgenticPDF demonstrates that streaming-first architecture and semantic-aware chunking significantly improve document intelligence for AI systems. The aPDF metadata envelope provides a standardized bridge between PDF documents and AI ecosystems, enabling automated workflows for paper discovery, artifact linking, and RAG pipeline construction. We release all code, models, and evaluation data to support further research.
